summary: The geometric-height measure is nonzero and finite, and the accepted weighted integer centerpoint theorem applies to its countable atomic support. Positive closed-halfspace depth forces every certified point into the canonical epigraph, including for lower-dimensional supports, so the mapped center and cutoff are admissible. The exact rounded geometric sums, vertical normals, and boundary atoms give the original-weight lower-cap comparison. For the stated quadratic box family, the tangent cap is exactly a lattice ball at every center; its Gaussian counting bound and the total-weight estimate yield the uniform small-cutoff bound. Splitting certified centers at L = n/20000 proves the asserted all-mesh obstruction for the certificate score. No mathematical errors or gaps were found, and the conclusion correctly distinguishes that certificate score from the actual hitting score.
